ANALYSIS: Tinea incognito is a dermatophyte infection whose clinical appearance has been altered by topical (or systemic) corticosteroids or immunosuppressants, often requiring recognition of steroid exposure, cessation of steroids, and sometimes different diagnostic suspicion/treatment duration. Labeling it simply "tinea corporis" does name the underlying infection but omits the important steroid‑modified presentation and management implications. These are not clinically equivalent.
